brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.evidence: notch:0#1,-1#notch4 (Notch drawer frame, hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) sits in the empty position at cell (1,-1), between the bases at (0,0), (1,0) and (0,-1).
spike:0#-1,0|0,-1|0,0 (solid spike) stands at the junction of cells (-1,0), (0,-1) and (0,0). mesh clear.

requirements.requirement: Drawer and spike at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: The configurator only offers a spike where three base cells meet, and a drawer occupies an empty cell position. Every corner point is shared by exactly three cells, so a drawer cell and a spike cannot share a corner point. Tried: spike at the corner of (0,0),(1,0),(1,-1) with the drawer put in (1,-1), which removed the spike; the drawer at (0,1) gave no spike offer. The drawer and spike in the final build are at different corners and do not touch.

finish.summary: I could place one notch drawer frame and one spike, but not at the same corner of the same cell. The configurator places a spike only where three base cells meet, and a drawer takes an empty cell position, so no corner is shared by both. The final build has the drawer at cell (1,-1) and the spike at the junction of (-1,0), (0,-1), (0,0), which are not touching. Mesh check is clear. Two half bases show LOOSE_BODY; joint bolts or lockJoints would fix that, but I did not run the house rules because the brief did not ask for them.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
